reason: The numerical chemistry supports IBr under the disclosed interpretation that X is an iodine-containing diatomic halogen/interhalogen adding intact once across each of the fatty acid’s two C=C bonds. The source, however, does not explicitly restrict X to the custom finite domain {IF, ICl, IBr, I2}; consequently the theorem establishes only conditional uniqueness within an unjustified search domain. The final theorem also hardcodes the preceding-part fatty-acid mass and addition stoichiometry rather than logically depending on the source-derived fatty-acid theorem.

coverage.evidence: The theorem proves `reagentFormula x = iodineMonobromideFormula` from membership in `IodineHalogenReagent` and the 36.57% measurement interval. `iodineBromide_matches_source` proves non-vacuous consistency and `iodineReagent_unique` proves uniqueness among IF, ICl, IBr, and I2. Independently, C18H32O2 has molar mass 280.436 g mol⁻¹, two IBr additions give 36.568708...% iodine, within [36.565%, 36.575%]. The conclusion is therefore correct only under the added reagent-domain and reaction-model conditions.

unsupported_assumptions: X is restricted to the four-constructor type `IodineHalogenReagent` containing only IF, ICl, IBr, and I2. The problem states only that X reacts similarly to iodine and does not supply this finite candidate domain.

“Reacts in similar way” is modeled as addition of two intact diatomic reagent molecules—one per C=C—with every reagent atom retained in the adduct. This is chemically plausible and disclosed, but not entailed explicitly by the source.

`adductIodineMassPercent` directly embeds the C18H32O2 molar mass and two-addition stoichiometry. `compound_x_formula` does not invoke or quantify over the source constraints proved separately by `fattyAcid_formula_from_all_source_constraints`.
source_checks: TASK.json was read first. SHA-256 values for the PDF and all three T5 page images match TASK.json.

Original PDF pages 44–46 and T5_page-1.png through T5_page-3.png were inspected directly. The fragment counts n, 2, 3, and 4; three equimolar ozonolysis products; 255 total sigma-plus-pi bonds; 181.0 g iodine per 100 g acid; and 36.57% iodine are accurately transcribed.
The blank A5-3 student answer sheet on PDF page 50 was inspected directly; it contains only blank fields for the preceding fatty acid and X and supplies no additional premise.
The supplied periodic table was inspected directly: H 1.008, C 12.01, O 16.00, F 19.00, Cl 35.45, Br 79.90, and I 126.9 agree with the candidate constants.

Independent reconstruction gives two C=C bonds, PL1 bond count 12n+39 = 255, n = 18, and fatty acid C18H32O2. Its calculated iodine uptake is 181.003865... g per 100 g, consistent with 181.0 g. Two IBr additions give 36.568708...% iodine, consistent with 36.57%.
